purpose: Frovatriptan is used to treat migraine headaches in adults, with or without the visual disturbances called aura. It helps relieve the pain, nausea, and sensitivity to light and sound that come with migraines. It is not used to prevent migraines or to treat other types of headaches.
how_it_works: When a migraine starts, certain blood vessels in your brain widen and become inflamed, causing that throbbing pain. Frovatriptan works by attaching to specific receptors in those blood vessels, causing them to narrow back to their normal size. It also helps block pain signals being sent to your brain, which helps relieve your migraine symptoms.
common_side_effects: Dizziness, tingling or numbness, feeling warm or flushed, headache, dry mouth, fatigue or tiredness, and an upset stomach. Some people also feel a brief tightness or pressure in the chest, neck, or jaw after taking it.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you have heart disease, a history of stroke or heart attack, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or certain types of migraines called hemiplegic or basilar migraines. Tell your doctor about all medications you take, especially antidepressants, as dangerous interactions can occur. Do not take more than two doses in 24 hours, and wait at least two hours between doses. Seek emergency help right away if you have severe chest pain, sudden severe headache, or signs of a stroke.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 2.5 mg tablet taken by mouth at the first sign of a migraine. If your headache comes back after it went away, you may take a second tablet, but wait at least 2 hours after the first dose. Do not take more than two tablets (5 mg total) in any 24-hour period.
